description: Architectural evaluation of three sensing alternatives to resolve the 0/38 secondary cross-aisle depth occlusion bottleneck.

options.architecture: Dedicated cross-aisle inward-facing optical cameras (Camera C) paired with entry threshold camera (Camera B)
what_it_observes: Rich 2D visual texture, human clothing, posture, and gaze orientation
Fine-grained actor classification (pedestrian, forklift driver, order picker, stationary obstacle)
Visual interactions with racking infrastructure (reaching, picking, leaning)
what_it_cannot_observe: Direct metric 3D depth without extrinsic homography or stereo disparity matching
Workers fully obscured behind floor-standing pallet stacks (> 2.0m height)
Visual targets under deep shadow or during aisle lighting shutdown

spatial_calibration_requirement.method: ArUco board calibration wand surveyed across overlapping Camera B and Camera C ground planes

failure_modes: Dust and grease accumulation on optical lens in high-traffic distribution centers
Direct glare from overhead high-bay LED fixtures blinding sensor at specific sun angles
YOLO detector misses on partially occluded crouching workers

options.architecture: Overhead 3D Solid-State LiDAR mounted at cross-aisle junction scanning 30m aisle volume
what_it_observes: Direct metric 3D point cloud of aisle volume with millimeter spatial accuracy
Velocity vectors and acceleration of all moving volumetric blobs independent of ambient lighting
Volumetric intrusion into aisle clearance boundaries in complete darkness
what_it_cannot_observe: Semantic actor identity (cannot reliably distinguish between a worker, a low-profile pallet jack, or fallen cargo without dense point density)
Targets behind dense shrink-wrapped pallet faces causing specular multi-path beam deflection
Absorptive dark clothing causing localized point dropouts

spatial_calibration_requirement.method: Iterative Closest Point (ICP) registration against retro-reflective calibration targets surveyed into facility CAD frame

failure_modes: Specular reflection flares off shiny plastic stretch-wrap on high pallets producing ghost points
Suspended dust clouds from forklift braking triggering false occupancy alerts
High per-aisle hardware and deployment cost across large facilities

options.architecture: Industrial Ultra-Wideband (UWB) personnel tags + vertical safety light curtains mounted across rack uprights
what_it_observes: Definitive sub-decimeter personnel micro-location for tagged warehouse staff
Binary planar perimeter intrusion detection via safety light curtains across aisle entrance
Zero dependency on optical line-of-sight, lighting conditions, or environmental dust
what_it_cannot_observe: Un-tagged individuals (visitors, delivery contractors, non-badged personnel)
Non-personnel physical hazards (fallen pallets, protruding forks, unattended machinery)
Continuous 2D/3D human body posture or evasive reaction dynamics

spatial_calibration_requirement.method: Total Station theodolite surveying of fixed UWB anchor positions and curtain optical emitter plane

failure_modes: Worker enters cross-aisle without assigned UWB wearable or with dead battery
Multipath RF reflections from corrugated metal siding causing position hopping
Accidental physical misalignment of light curtain beams by forklift mast bumps
